findings.how_to_check: Run python replication/check_claims.py --paper-repo D:\repos\6638fa0fd89fbec05130caeb; observe assertion failures on intro-val-gain (line 98), results-validated (line 548), and results-all (line 551).
findings.suggested_fix: Re-run create_figures_SSHA2025.do via replication/run_machineA.do to regenerate figures/avg_performance_allstates.tex and results/create_figures_SSHA2025.tex. Update lines 68, 98, 548, and 551 in DHTS-2026-10-12.tex to report 16% (increasing from 64% to 75%) for target records and ~0% / 0.1% for the full sample.
findings.title: The paper and headline Table 4 report superseded moving-validator validation gains of 28% rather than 16%
findings.what_the_code_does: The uncommitted changes in create_figures_SSHA2025.do:81-98 replace file-specific 1940 middle initials with Ancestry's fixed initial mi1940_anc for both before and after validation. As documented in validation_fixed_initials.do:70-71 and results/validation_fixed_initials.tex:28-32, the fixed initial reduces the target-sample validation gain from +27.8% (+28%) to +16.0% (from 64.3% to 74.5%), and the full-sample validation gain from +1.3% (+1%) to +0.07% (+0.1%). The paper draft (lines 68, 98, 548, 551), Table 4 (avg_performance_allstates.tex:10-11), and result macros still report the outdated 28%, 65% to 84%, and 1% numbers.
findings.why_it_matters: The abstract, introduction, and Section 5 headline results overstate the match-quality improvement by 12 percentage points (28% vs 16%) and report an overall validation increase of 1% that is essentially 0% (+0.07%) under the fixed validator. Referees will find that the reported validation numbers fail to reproduce from the code.

findings.how_to_check: Evaluate the assertion expression in Python using the raw values from validation_fixed_initials.tex: '15.95187 <= 11.50597 + 1', which returns False.
findings.suggested_fix: Update lines 76 and 361 in replication/claims.toml to test equality against the chosen Ancestry benchmark (e.g. 'abs(valGainTarget - valGainAncTarget) < 1.0') and retire the moving-validator issue note once verified.
findings.title: Claim registry assertion intro-val-gain and results-validated will fail even after draft numbers are updated to 16%
findings.what_the_code_does: In replication/claims.toml:76,361, the assertions for intro-val-gain and results-validated require 'valGainTarget <= valGainAncTarget + 1 and valGainTarget <= valGainFsTarget + 1'. While valGainTarget will now match valGainAncTarget (~15.95%), valGainFsTarget is 11.51%. Because 15.95 <= 12.51 is false, the second conjunct fails regardless of what number the draft quotes.
findings.why_it_matters: Even after rebuilding the data and updating the draft text to 16%, check_claims.py will exit with code 1, breaking automated CI/replication and obscuring other verification checks.

findings.how_to_check: After rebuilding temp.dta, inspect socioGroupsNotImproved in replication/results/create_figures_SSHA2025.tex and check whether any point in the lower panel of all_states_socio_demo_combinedV2.pdf falls on or below y=0.
findings.suggested_fix: After re-running create_figures_SSHA2025.do, inspect the 65 subgroup validation changes. If any subgroup has v9 <= 0, qualify lines 728-729 and 740 in DHTS-2026-10-12.tex to state that while linkage rates improved for every group, middle-initial validation improvements are concentrated in discordant records while full-sample validation rates remain steady at parity across groups.
findings.title: Fixed-initial validation gain of +0.07% full-sample threatens claim that every socio-demographic group improved
findings.what_the_code_does: create_figures_SSHA2025.do:409-410 counts socioGroupsNotImproved where subgroup linkage gain v8 <= 0 or validation gain v9 <= 0. Under the old moving validator, valGainAll was +1.34% and all 65 groups had v9 > 0. Under the fixed Ancestry initial, full-sample valGainAncAll is only +0.07%, making it likely that normal variation pushes some subgroup validation gains to zero or below, yet DHTS-2026-10-12.tex lines 729 and 740 claim 'Every group improved on both measures, so each panel\'s vertical axis lies entirely above zero' and 'no group saw its linkage rate or validation rate decline'.
findings.why_it_matters: If any subgroup has v9 <= 0 after the rebuild, socioGroupsNotImproved will exceed 0, contradicting the text, violating the caption of Figure 4, and failing the socio-all-improved and no-group-fell assertions in claims.toml.

findings.how_to_check: Execute '.\replication\Run-MachineA.ps1 -SkipRebuild' before rebuilding temp.dta; inspect the log for r(9) at line 84 of validation_fixed_initials.do.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a check or warning in Run-MachineA.ps1 detecting when temp.dta is older than create_figures_SSHA2025.do or contains legacy validation flags, disallowing -SkipRebuild until a clean full rebuild has succeeded.
findings.title: Running replication with -SkipRebuild crashes validation_fixed_initials.do on un-rebuilt temp.dta
findings.what_the_code_does: validation_fixed_initials.do:83-84 asserts 'assert vb_anc==validated_before' and 'assert va_anc==validated_after' against temp.dta. When Run-MachineA.ps1 is invoked with -SkipRebuild, create_figures_SSHA2025.do is omitted, leaving the legacy temp.dta where validated_after reflects mi1940_new rather than mi1940_anc (~4.6% mismatch). Stata halts with return code 9.
findings.why_it_matters: The documented fast-path -SkipRebuild option fails with an unhandled fatal assertion error whenever temp.dta has not yet been regenerated following this code change.

findings.suggested_fix: Discuss the choice of 1940 benchmark initial in Section 5 or the Table 4 note, explicitly presenting the FamilySearch fixed initial (11.5%) as a robustness check to prove that the validation gain is not driven by the choice of human comparator.
findings.title: Evaluating ML-generated links against Ancestry's middle initial introduces source asymmetry
findings.what_the_code_does: create_figures_SSHA2025.do:81-98 evaluates both Ancestry links (Before) and ML links (After) using mi1940_anc extracted from Ancestry's 1940 first name. If Ancestry mis-transcribed the 1940 first-name field, its middle initial is missing or erroneous. In replication/results/validation_fixed_initials.tex, using FamilySearch's fixed initial (valGainFsTarget) yields an 11.5% gain, compared to 16.0% under Ancestry's initial.
findings.why_it_matters: Choosing Ancestry's initial as the single reference standard produces a 4.5 percentage point higher gain than FamilySearch's initial due to differences in baseline agreement (64.3% vs 72.9%). Without documenting or justifying this choice alongside FamilySearch robustness, the finding is vulnerable to referee challenge on benchmark sensitivity.

review_limits: The Stata replication pipeline was not executed in this session; findings are based on static code tracing, git diffs, tracked diagnostic outputs, and paper artifacts.
Underlying census and linkage datasets (residing on external drives) could not be queried directly to independently verify record-level properties.
The exact effect of the fixed-initial update on the 65 socio-demographic subgroups (v9) cannot be confirmed until create_figures_SSHA2025.do completes a full multi-hour rebuild.
The upstream external linking scripts that originally generated the 1930-1940 link files are not part of this repository.
structured_output.summary: The switch to Ancestry's fixed 1940 middle initial in `create_figures_SSHA2025.do` resolves an asymmetric moving validator, but leaves the paper draft, headline Table 4, and result macros reporting superseded gains of 28% (instead of 16%) for discordant records and 1% (instead of ~0.1%) overall. Re-running the pipeline and updating the draft text and Table 4 is the submission-blocking priority. In addition, the claim registry's hardcoded assertions and the paper's claim of universal subgroup validation gains must be updated to avoid persistent automated check failures.

verified_clean.evidence: Both flags strictly require non-empty strings before evaluating equality: `mi`beg_yr'!="" & mi1940_anc!=""` at CODE/create_figures_SSHA2025.do:88,98.
verified_clean.item: Empty string comparisons in validation flags

verified_clean.evidence: `jr`, `sr`, `ii`, `iii`, `iv` are stripped of periods and blanked at CODE/create_figures_SSHA2025.do:83 and replication/diagnostics/validation_fixed_initials.do:27-28.

`assert validated_before==validated_after if linked_before==1 & linked_after==1 & id_A_before==id_A` at CODE/create_figures_SSHA2025.do:101 guarantees that links pairing the same records across censuses receive identical validation verdicts before and after.

Links are decomposed into kept, switched, added, and dropped categories in replication/diagnostics/validation_fixed_initials.do:59-62,100-112 to ensure quality gains reflect genuine accuracy on added links rather than compositional churn.
The manuscript explicitly distinguishes agreement between human transcribers from truth, describing concordance as resemblance rather than reliability at DHTS-2026-10-12.tex:105,303.
verified_clean.item: Separation of commercial transcription agreement from ground truth

verified_clean.evidence: Middle initials are excluded from the matching algorithm (which uses first/last name, birth year, birthplace) at DHTS-2026-10-12.tex:407-408, preserving middle initials as an independent validation metric.
verified_clean.item: Exclusion of middle initials from linkage algorithm

summary.description: Two to four sentences. The overall state of the reviewed work and the single most important thing to fix. No preamble.

dimensions_reviewed.description: Which scope dimensions were actually reviewed in this run.

findings.description: Defects and concerns, ordered most severe first. Empty if none. Do not pad with stylistic observations.

severity.description: blocker: a reported result is wrong. major: a referee would demand it. minor: real but survivable. nit: cosmetic.

confidence.description: verified: traced in the source. likely: strongly implied but depends on unseen data. speculative: a question, not an established defect.

title.description: One line, stating the defect itself, not its category.

location.description: path:line, or path:line-line. Several may be comma-separated. Required: a finding without a location is not a finding.

what_the_code_does.description: Precisely what the code computes, quoting the relevant expression. Contrast with what it was evidently intended to compute.

why_it_matters.description: The consequence for a number or claim in the paper. If there is no consequence, the severity is nit.

how_to_check.description: A concrete command, tabulation, or count the author can run to confirm or refute this in minutes.

suggested_fix.description: The change, specific enough to act on. Do not apply it yourself.

verified_clean.description: Things explicitly checked that were fine. This is what makes a short findings list trustworthy rather than lazy.

evidence.description: How it was confirmed, with path:line where applicable.

review_limits.description: What this review could NOT establish: data not readable, pipeline not runnable, paper text unavailable, Stata semantics not verifiable by reading. Be explicit; silence here reads as false assurance.
